paper_title: NExtLong Toward Effective Long-Context Training without Long Documents
caption: NExtLong reduces the model's dependence on proximal text. We calculated the degree of dependence on proximal text (the last third of the text) for different methods when completing the LongQA task. It can be observed that NExtLong significantly reduces the model's dependence on proximal text.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the "Attention Weight" for short-dependence attention across five different methods—Standard, ICLM, KNN, Quest, and NExtLong—when performing the LongQA task. The horizontal axis, labeled "Methods," lists the five methods in left-to-right order, while the vertical axis, labeled "Attention Weight," is scaled from 0.80 to 0.90 with tick marks at 0.82, 0.84, 0.86, and 0.88, indicating a linear scale. Each method is represented by a single light blue bar, corresponding to the "Short-Dependence Attention Weight" as indicated in the legend. The attention weights for Standard, ICLM, KNN, and Quest are approximately 0.86, 0.84, 0.86, and 0.86, respectively, while NExtLong has a significantly lower attention weight of approximately 0.82. The bars are arranged in a simple horizontal layout with no grouping or stacking, and the chart includes light gray gridlines for easier value estimation. The visual data supports the claim that NExtLong reduces the model's dependence on proximal text compared to the other methods, as its bar is visibly shorter than all others.
